ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Jack London

code.originalText: Two-week review after stopping alcohol and starting losartan, seen the same day by nephrology: kidney staging and cause, ultrasound and elastography, blood pressure target, medicine for alcohol use disorder, and pain relief

text.paragraph: Two-week review after stopping alcohol and starting losartan, seen the same day by nephrology. [S]

Mr. London stopped drinking on the morning after his intake visit and took the five-day chlordiazepoxide taper as prescribed, with a daily telephone check from the nurse. The first three days brought sweats, a tremor and poor sleep, at worst a CIWA-Ar of 11 on the second day, with no hallucinations or seizures; by the fifth day the tremor had gone, and he has had no alcohol since. He missed two mornings of writing and has written his thousand words every other day. He has taken losartan 50 mg daily without dizziness and stopped naproxen; acetaminophen eases his knee. His ankles are less swollen. He has seen the clinic's addiction counselor once. The insurance examination report has arrived, confirming a creatinine of 1.7 mg/dL about fourteen months ago. Ultrasound and liver elastography were done this morning. He sees Dr. Mbatha-Rasmussen of nephrology this afternoon. [S]

list.item:
Chronic kidney disease G3b A2 (N18.32). Dr. Mbatha-Rasmussen confirms chronic kidney disease: a creatinine of 1.7 mg/dL fourteen months ago and 1.98 now, eGFR 42 to 43 and urine albumin 240 mg/g. Normal-sized echogenic kidneys without stones or obstruction and a bland urine sediment point to hypertensive kidney disease with a contribution from two years of daily naproxen; a biopsy is not needed now. Five-year kidney failure risk about 5 percent. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV serology drawn today. [S]
Continue losartan; raise to 100 mg at six weeks if potassium allows.
Dapagliflozin once he has been abstinent for some weeks and is eating regularly.
25-hydroxyvitamin D, missed at intake, with the next blood test.
Nephrology review in three months.

Hypertensive chronic kidney disease (I12.9). 146/92, from 158/98. Target below 120 systolic by standardized measurement if tolerated. [S]
Less salt; home readings.

Alcohol use disorder, severe (F10.20). Withdrawal completed safely; twelve days without alcohol. With Dr. Mbatha-Rasmussen he chose naltrexone, which needs no dose change at his kidney function, over acamprosate, which would need a lower dose at his creatinine clearance of about 58 mL/min and three doses a day. Liver tests are falling and well under three times normal; no opioid use. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; firearms locked; 988 card carried. [S]
Naltrexone 50 mg every morning from today, with a wallet card.
Counseling weekly; continue thiamine.

Alcohol-associated fatty liver (K70.0). FIB-4 2.28 was indeterminate; liver stiffness 7.2 kPa makes advanced fibrosis unlikely, though stiffness can read high soon after heavy drinking. Abstinence is the treatment. [S]
Liver tests at six weeks.

Naproxen use (Z79.1). Stopped; acetaminophen is controlling the knee pain. [S]
No oral anti-inflammatory medicines.
